Done. Deliverables are in `~`:

- **`github-actions-billing-failed-job-not-started.md`** — the full solution (title, root-cause analysis, detection recipe, exact fix, verification, guardrail).
- **`diagnose-billing-job-not-started.sh`** — one-shot triage script automating the detection recipe; validated with `bash -n` and correct usage/exit handling (`exit=2` on missing args).

## Summary

**Diagnosis:** Jobs fail in ~2 s with `steps: []`, `started_at ≈ completed_at`, empty `--log-failed`, and log API `BlobNotFound` because GitHub never started the runner. The only cause is in the **run annotations**: *"The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased."*

**Root cause:** Account/org billing block — failed payment method or Actions spending limit at $0 (or exhausted included minutes on a private repo). Nothing in the workflow YAML is involved.

**Fix (account-side, never code):**
- Personal: `github.com/settings/billing` → fix payment method → raise/remove Actions spending limit → Save.
- Org: org owner at `github.com/organizations/ORG/settings/billing` (same steps).
- Re-run: `gh run rerun <run-id> --failed`.

**Verification:** After the fix, a job shows `step_count > 0`, a real runtime (not ~2 s), populated `steps`, real logs, and no billing annotation.

The doc also contains a guardrail against filing a code CI-fix task, since this class is always billing/account-side.
